hero.tituloDestacado: without depending on the operating system
hero.descripcion: SolarisPKN-Control is a remote power-on/power-off system built on ESP32 and Arduino IoT Cloud. It physically simulates the motherboard's Power SW button, so it keeps working even if the operating system is frozen or unresponsive.

filosofia.label: Philosophy
filosofia.quote: If the software freezes, the hardware still answers.

items.label: Power on
items.texto: Simulates a normal Power button press — turns the PC on, or triggers a graceful shutdown if the OS supports it.

items.label: Forced shutdown
items.texto: Holds the signal for 15 seconds to force a shutdown, exactly like holding the physical button on the case.

items.label: Efficiency
items.texto: ESP32 CPU underclocked from 240 to 80 MHz, Bluetooth disabled, and WiFi in power-save mode — built to run 24/7 without wasting power.

items.label: Independence
items.texto: No installation needed on the operating system. All the logic lives on the ESP32, isolated from the machine it controls.

architecture.label: Architecture
architecture.titulo: How the signal reaches the case

items.name: Arduino IoT Cloud
items.desc: Remote control from the official dashboard or mobile app, without exposing any ports of your own to the internet.

items.name: VPN + Sunshine/Moonlight
items.desc: Paired with desktop streaming for full remote access: power the PC on and connect straight into the session, without exposing it directly to the internet.

security.label: Security
items: No direct electrical connection between the ESP32 and the motherboard — the relay isolates both circuits.
Doesn't rely on remote-access software (RDP, VNC) on the operating system, reducing the controlled machine's attack surface.
Recommended remote access is always via VPN (WireGuard/Tailscale), never exposing ports directly to the internet.
Power-on/off authentication is delegated to Arduino IoT Cloud, not to a self-hosted, exposed server.

cta.descripcion: The project is open source under the MIT license, with full documentation and wiring diagrams available in the GitHub repository.
